question_en:
I am organizing a batch of county-level electronic sample ballots and preparing to add an "automatically skip blank back sides" feature to the accessible lookup system. The current test rule treats page 2 of every PDF as blank; if page 2 still contains voting items, the system will miss the entire page's content. Please answer the following questions:

1. Which election and which type of sample ballot does the input image represent? Please provide the county name, election date, sample ballot version number, and, based on the official materials for that election, determine the complete voting area identifier applicable to this sample ballot.
2. Review all versions of the sample ballot PDFs officially released for this election. For which sample ballots does page 2 still contain voting content? The criterion for determination is that page 2 simultaneously displays the gray header bar for voting items and the rectangular selection boxes below it; pages containing only diagonal watermarks or text stating "intentionally left blank" do not count. How many sample ballot versions were released in total for this election? How many of them meet the above conditions? Please list the version numbers of all matching sample ballots.

Response Format: Please answer in points numbered (1)—(2); answer both questions in text. For question 1, provide four identification items. For question 2, provide the total number of sample ballots, the number of matches, and all matching version numbers.
answer:
(1) County Name: Hidalgo County; Election Date: May 3, 2025; Sample Ballot Version Number (Ballot Style): 10; Complete Voting Area Identifier (precinct-split): 040-02.

(2) There are 18 sample ballot versions in total; 6 versions still have voting content on page 2, with version numbers 04, 10, 12, 15, 17, and 18.
